findings.description: publicly_accessible = true assigns the MySQL RDS instance a publicly resolvable endpoint, so the database is reachable from outside the VPC rather than only from the application subnet.
storage_encrypted = false leaves the RDS storage, automated snapshots and backups unencrypted, so data at rest is readable by anyone with access to the storage layer.

The master password is supplied as var.password and interpolated into the EC2 user_data script, rendered into Terraform state, and written in cleartext to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc on the instance, exposing the DB credential; the password is also excluded from rotation via lifecycle ignore_changes.

The user_data heredoc embeds the database password (var.password) and master username directly into an include file written to the web root, exposing credentials via instance metadata, Terraform state, and the disk/webroot of a publicly reachable host.

The policy attached to the EC2-assumable role grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", so compromise of the publicly reachable web server yields full control of account storage, compute and databases, violating least privilege.
The generated PHP application connects to MySQL without TLS, transmitting the database username and password and all query data in cleartext across the network between the web server and RDS.
MySQL port 3306 is opened to the entire portal VPC CIDR rather than scoped to the application security group, letting any workload in the VPC reach the database.
The database security group permits all protocols to 0.0.0.0/0, providing no egress restriction and enabling data exfiltration or reverse connections if the database host is compromised.
The master account name is hard-coded as the well-known privileged name "admin", simplifying credential-guessing against the publicly reachable database.
